2: This Ordinance shall be known as the "1999 General Election Ordinance for the Town of Clermont, Georgia."
3: The Town of Clermont, Georgia will conduct a General Election on Tuesday, November 2, 1999, from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m., with the place of said election being in the Town Hall, 122 Dean Street, Clermont, Georgia 30527 for the public positions as indicated in
6: O.C.G.A. § 21-2-135(a)(2) [1999 Amendment] provides that regarding elections involving two or more public offices, each having the same title and to be filled at the same election by the vote of the same electors, that the Town Charter or pursuant to ordinance by the Town Council, may require for candidates to designate the specific office the candidate is seeking by incumbent or post, or both. The Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia does hereby find that it is in the best interests of the citizens and electors of the Town of Clermont, for candidates to not designate the office the candidate is seeking, which would eliminate personal attacks upon candidates for seats upon the Town Council, and be in accordance with the Town Charter.
8:
The General Election to be held on the date established by Section 2 hereof this

Ordinance is to fill the following offices:

(A) The office of Town Councilmember of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, which will be elected at large for a term of four (4) years beginning on January 1, 2000 through December 31, 2003, with said seat currently held by Steve Gailey.

(B) The office of Town Councilmember of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, which will be elected at large for a term of four (4) years beginning on January 1, 2000 through December 31, 2003, with said seat currently held by Orville Nolan.

(C) The office of Town Councilmember of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, which will be elected at large for a term of four (4) years beginning on January 1, 2000 through December 31, 2003, with said seat currently held by Gaylard Kesler.
9: The qualifying period for the election set by Section 2 of this Ordinance to qualify for the offices set by Section 4 of this Ordinance, shall open on Monday, September 13, 1999, and will continue from day-to-day through Thursday, September 16, 1999. The hours of qualifying each day shall be from 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. (except for a one hour lunch break beginning at 1:00 p.m. each day). The place of qualifying shall be the administrative office of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, being one of the offices of the Election Superintendent, and being located at the Town Hall, 122 Dean Street, Clermont, Georgia 30527.
10:
(A) The qualifying fee for the positions open for election as provided by Section 4 of this Ordinance shall be $21.60 for each of the Council seats. Such fee shall be paid to the Election Superintendent at the time a candidate files the candidate's application and notice of candidacy.

(B) A pauper's affidavit may be filed in lieu of paying the qualifying fee otherwise required by this Ordinance in Section 6(A). A candidate filing a pauper's affidavit instead of paying a qualifying fee shall under oath affirm the candidate's poverty and the candidate's resulting inability to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The form of the affidavit shall be as prescribed by the Georgia Secretary of State and shall include a financial statement which lists the total income, assets, liabilities, and other relevant financial information of the candidate and shall indicate on its face that the candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The affidavit shall contain an oath that such candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required. The following warning shall be printed on the affidavit form as prepared by the Georgia Secretary of State, to wit! "WARNING: Any person knowingly making any false statement on this affidavit commits the offense of false swearing and shall be guilty of a felony." The Election Superintendent shall place on the ballot the name of any candidate who subscribes and swears to an oath that such candidate has neither the assets nor the income to pay the qualifying fee otherwise required.
